methodology.scope: The initial denominator combines the dominant volume resins with established engineering thermoplastics, thermosets, elastomers, fibers, natural and semisynthetic polymers, degradable and biomedical materials, and a representative functional-polymer tail. Families and processing-relevant subfamilies may both appear because they answer different research questions.
selectionSignals: Documented presence among dominant global resin groups
Repeated treatment in open polymer textbooks or university courseware
Distinct industrial processing, cure, spinning, or vulcanization behavior
Established engineering, high-temperature, barrier, elastomeric, biomedical, or functional use
Recognized polymer class or source-based name in public nomenclature references
methodology.rankingDisclaimer: This is a curated high-priority coverage set, not a quantitative worldwide production ranking. Public market sources resolve the largest resin groups but aggregate much of the long tail.
methodology.sourceStandard: Methodology sources justify the catalog boundary and vocabulary only. They do not support unwritten claims in individual stubs. Article prose must later be mapped to its own anonymously accessible sources.
